tools.name: create_mailbox
tools.description: Create a disposable receivemail.dev email address that receives real mail. Returns address, expiresAt and secret; keep the secret to read the mailbox. Free without a key (up to 60 minutes); with a paid key on the MCP connection, up to 1440 minutes and an extracted otp field on messages.

tools.name: wait_for_email
tools.description: Wait up to 25 seconds for an email to a mailbox made with create_mailbox. Returns {timed_out:false, message:{from_address, subject, body_text, received_at}} or {timed_out:true}; call again on timeout. Pass `since` (ISO 8601) to ignore mail you've already seen.

tools.name: list_messages
tools.description: List the last 50 emails received by a mailbox made with create_mailbox, newest first.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_mailbox" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_mailbox, list_messages · Private data: create_mailbox · Public sink: create_mailbox, wait_for_email.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_mailbox, list_messages · Private data: create_mailbox · Public sink: create_mailbox, wait_for_email

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
